decisions: Lead with the concrete agenda and reservation problem; Turnos owns the hero and first product section.
Preserve the warm editorial system, React section ownership, native mailto contract and visible email fallbacks.
Compress Backoffice, services and academy into a secondary ecosystem; remove repeated brand exposition before adding detail.
boundaries: Hero owns navigation, the primary Turnos promise, one general-email CTA, one in-page CTA and the first product proof.
Turnos owns benefits, the daily-agenda visual and a pilot-founder inquiry without unconfirmed availability claims.
About owns a compact three-step working method and no separate brand-manifesto canvas.
Offer owns Backoffice plus implementation, custom software and academy as secondary paths.
Faq and Footer own objection handling and the two visible direct email destinations; no form or provider selector.
states: The landing is static and has no loading, empty, submit-disabled or success state.
Mailto links expose visible fallback addresses because native-client availability is outside application control.
All layouts must reflow from 320px through wide desktop without horizontal overflow or decorative dead space.
verification: DevTeam schema v3 state validates with the schema-v3 prepare receipt bound to FurcodeTech/landing.
Live repository owner, develop base and prepared local branch were rechecked before the first write.
Existing local render was inspected at 390x844 and wide desktop with zero horizontal overflow and no sub-44px targets.
residual_risks: The formal FurcodeUI router has no Vite surface, so implementation uses the direct React Taller doctrine and the retained Vite readiness capability.
Turnos commercial availability, pricing, pilot capacity and real inbox delivery remain outside local evidence.
not_verified: Native mail-client handoff and external email receipt.
Any claim about open pilot slots, price or launch date.
